requirement: Annex J is headed Informative, but our profile CSMA Fixed Frequency makes Annex J mandatory. Reading: every shall in Annex J is binding on us, and its shoulds are followed where they apply.
notes: Ed4 main 7.2 Table 2, p.13; plan 4.1. Ed4 K.5, p.K-13 says Annex K became Optional to align with Annex J, yet J is still headed Informative.

requirement: The enhanced MAC modes extend or modify the Annex B channel-access and link-control mechanisms but do not replace them; CAS-1 linking stays in force.
notes: Introductory text; the J.1 heading is missing from the PDF.

requirement: Layer model: a Media-Access Control Sublayer (MACS) sits below the Annex C DTS and above the modem; extra MAC functions may be placed in it (Figure J-1).
notes: Figure J-1 also shows a modem status line (for example DCD) into the MAC. For CSMA the MAC only manages access timers [Ed4 C, p.C-122].

requirement: Added MAC functionality must be built on the D_PDU types defined in Annex C.
notes: Annex K CSMA adds no D_PDU types [Ed4 K.1, p.K-1].

requirement: A MAC may define additional D_PDU types of its own for media-access control.
reason: we define no new D_PDU types; Annex K CSMA needs none [Ed4 K.1, p.K-1]

requirement: Any new MAC D_PDU type must follow the Annex C message-definition rules, the generic D_PDU frame structure and the D_PDU field-element rules (cited as Annex C C.3.1 and C.3.2).
reason: we define no new D_PDU types; Annex K CSMA needs none [Ed4 K.1, p.K-1]
notes: Annex J cites Annex C C.3.1 and C.3.2 from the older numbering; in Ed4 these are C.4.1 (generic simplified D_PDU structure, p.C-9) and C.4.2 (generic detailed D_PDU structure, p.C-10).

requirement: New MAC function in a new D_PDU type must be confined to its type-specific header and, if present, its payload.
reason: we define no new D_PDU types; Annex K CSMA needs none [Ed4 K.1, p.K-1]

requirement: New MAC D_PDU types may carry only peer-to-peer MACS traffic between nodes.
reason: we define no new D_PDU types; Annex K CSMA needs none [Ed4 K.1, p.K-1]
notes: Figure J-2, p.J-2.

requirement: Client traffic and the peer exchanges of Annexes A, B and C keep using the D_PDU types defined in Annex C.
The MAC must leave the Annex A S_PDU and Annex B C_PDU definitions unchanged.
MACS functionality may be tailored using the mode options of J.3 to suit multi-node networks.
notes: We use the CSMA mode only (plan 4.1).

requirement: Four MAC modes are defined: point-to-point (P2P), CSMA, WTRP and ATDMA; their detailed requirements live in the cross-referenced annexes.
notes: List before J.3.1; the J.3 heading is missing from the PDF.

requirement: P2P mode lets a pair of nodes hold the channel for traffic between just the two of them.
Default point-to-point channel access must follow Annex B (for us, CAS-1 linking without ALE).
notes: Plan 4.3 ALE row; Ed4 B.7, p.B-12.

requirement: Point-to-point operation must also use CSMA per Annex K, even when only two nodes are involved.
notes: See J-0068 (Annex J versus Annex R) and matrix/K.tsv. Listed as an Ed4 change on p.J-9.

requirement: For two nodes some simplification of the Annex K procedure is possible; Annex J does not say which.
notes: See J-0069 and K-0109.

requirement: CSMA mode lets a set of nodes share one channel by sensing the carrier and transmitting only when the node believes the channel is clear.
If a CSMA mode is implemented it must follow Annex K.
notes: matrix/K.tsv.

requirement: Annex K CSMA uses only the Edition 1 D_PDU catalogue and the basic Annex A, B and C capabilities, with augmented Annex D requirements for listen-before-transmit.
notes: See J-0020 on the Annex D part.

requirement: J.3.2 says Annex K relies on augmented Annex D requirements for listen-before-transmit, but Ed4 Annex D contains no carrier-detect or listen-before-transmit requirement, and we do not implement the Annex D interface (plan 4.3). Reading: carrier sense comes from our own modem port, the demodulator carrier detect as DCD and received EOTs as VDCD (plan 7.2); nothing further is taken from Annex D.
notes: Ed4 D, p.D-1 (no mention of DCD, carrier or listen anywhere in Annex D); plan 4.4 Annex D row. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: WTRP mode shares the channel by passing a right-to-transmit token round a ring of nodes; the holder transmits until it has no more data or its timer expires.
reason: WTRP (Annex L) is not in our profile (plan 4.3)

requirement: WTRP mode must be implemented per Annex L.
reason: WTRP (Annex L) is not in our profile (plan 4.3)

requirement: WTRP D_PDUs are new types carried as EXTENSION D_PDUs (type 13), with the WTRP fields in the D_PDU-specific part.
notes: Needed to recognise WTRP traffic for the WARNING of J-0039. Annex L assigns extended types 1 to 4 (INVITE, JOIN, TABLE, TABLE+) [Ed4 L, Table L-1, p.L-18]; Annex C passes extended types 1 to 6 to WTRP [Ed4 C.7.5.1, p.C-110] while C.8 lists 1 to 4 [p.C-124]; plan 4.4. The WTRP token itself is an EOW, not a D_PDU type: J-0070.

requirement: ATDMA would divide the channel into adaptive timeslots and would need new management D_PDUs; no STANAG 5066 annex specifies TDMA or ATDMA.
reason: ATDMA is unspecified and not in our profile

requirement: All MAC modes share the generic Annex C D_PDU structure, so any compliant node can decode the common fields of any D_PDU, in particular its source address and D_PDU type, even for a MAC it does not implement.
notes: Text after J.3.4; the J.4 heading is missing. We must parse the header of an EXTENSION D_PDU to address a WARNING to its sender.

requirement: The MAC modes are not interoperable with one another; operating procedures are expected to keep a single MAC protocol per network.
Annex J provides discovery so that a node can at least recognise an incompatible MAC in use and act to avoid mutual interference.
MAC-Mode Discovery is the name for the processes by which nodes find out which MAC modes are in use on a network.
Nodes should implement MAC-Mode Discovery, made up of the WARNING-message element (J.4.1.1) and the channel-analysis element (J.4.1.2).
The mandatory Annex C WARNING (type 15) D_PDU provisions apply to MAC-Mode Discovery, as amplified in J.4.1.1.
notes: Annex J cites Annex C C.3.12 from the older numbering; in Ed4 the WARNING D_PDU is C.4.15 [Ed4 C.4.15, pp.C-54 to C-56].

requirement: A node running a MAC mode must analyse other nodes' channel use for violations of its own protocol and act on them, including sending WARNINGs to tell neighbours of the incompatibility.
notes: Restated in J.4.1.2 (J-0043). Actions: J-0051.

requirement: Annex C already requires a node that receives an unexpected or unknown D_PDU to send a WARNING D_PDU to its originator; the MAC modes do not change that.
notes: Ed4 C.4.15, p.C-54 shall (1) and p.C-56 shall (9).

requirement: On receiving a D_PDU that its own MAC protocol does not expect, or that it does not know, a node works out who sent it from the source address and sends that node a WARNING D_PDU.
notes: Text says 'will'; treated as shall because it restates Annex C. Such D_PDUs may indicate a node on a different MAC protocol. Addressing scope: J-0053.

requirement: The WARNING's RECEIVED FRAME TYPE field carries the D_PDU type number of the unexpected or unknown D_PDU.
notes: 4-bit field [Ed4 C, p.C-55]; for an EXTENSION D_PDU it is 13 and the extended type cannot be carried.

requirement: If the node does not recognise the D_PDU, REASON WARNING SENT is set to the 'Unrecognised D_PDU type' value.
notes: Value 0 [Ed4 C Table C-3, p.C-55]. See J-0052 for extension types.

requirement: A type 6 MANAGEMENT D_PDU whose EOW type (acting as a subtype for extended management messages) is not recognised is treated as an unrecognised D_PDU and draws a WARNING as above.
notes: See J-0054 for the overlap with the Annex C UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR EOW.

requirement: If the node recognises the D_PDU but it is unexpected for the protocol in use, REASON WARNING SENT is set to the 'Invalid D_PDU Received for Current State' value.
notes: Value 3 [Ed4 C Table C-3, p.C-55].

requirement: A type 6 D_PDU whose subtype is recognised but belongs to a MAC protocol the node is not running is treated as unexpected and draws a WARNING with the 'Invalid D_PDU Received for Current State' reason.
A P2P or CSMA node must answer every Annex L WTRP D_PDU type it receives with a WARNING as above, recognised or not.
notes: Plan 4.3 Annex L row. WTRP D_PDU types are EXTENSION D_PDUs with extended types 1 to 4 [Ed4 L, Table L-1, p.L-18]. Reason value: J-0052. Addressing scope: J-0053. Token EOWs: J-0070.

requirement: WARNINGs are possible only when the node both receives and transmits; a transmit-only node (for example one serving only an Annex A broadcast data exchange session) never receives D_PDUs that would trigger one.
A receive-only node cannot send WARNINGs, so it disables its protocol-error detection and WARNING generation.
notes: Applies to any receive-only configuration we offer; whether we offer one is NOT STATED here.

requirement: Nodes running different MAC modes transmit without coordinating, so they may interfere with each other.
A node must analyse the D_PDUs it receives from other nodes to detect violations of the MAC protocol it runs.
notes: Same duty as J-0031.

requirement: That analysis includes processing received WARNING D_PDUs per Annex C and J.4.1.1.
notes: Text cites 'Section J.2.1.1'; see J-0045.

requirement: J.4.1.2 refers to a 'Section J.2.1.1', which does not exist. Reading: it means J.4.1.1 (use of type 15 WARNING messages).
notes: Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: Traffic that contains none of the WTRP D_PDU types recognisable to the receiver should be taken as coming from a node currently in P2P or CSMA mode; this indicates its current mode, not its capability.
A WARNING whose RECEIVED FRAME TYPE is a WTRP D_PDU type and whose reason says unrecognised should be taken as coming from a node that can run only P2P or CSMA.
notes: See J-0050 on what RECEIVED FRAME TYPE can hold.

requirement: Such a node should be presumed to be a legacy (Edition 1) implementation that cannot run WTRP or ATDMA.
A WARNING reporting unexpected use of a WTRP D_PDU type should be taken as coming from a node running a different MAC mode from the node the WARNING is addressed to.
notes: See J-0050.

requirement: The 'unexpected use' bullet gives the reason field as unrecognised, the same as the preceding 'ignorance' bullet, which would make the two cases indistinguishable. Also, WTRP D_PDUs are EXTENSION D_PDUs, so RECEIVED FRAME TYPE can only show 13. Reading: a WARNING with RECEIVED FRAME TYPE 13 and reason 0 or 4 is the 'unrecognised' case; RECEIVED FRAME TYPE 13 with reason 3 (Invalid D_PDU Received for Current State) is the 'unexpected use' case, matching J.4.1.1.
notes: Ed4 C Table C-3, p.C-55. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: Annex J asks for appropriate action on detecting an incompatible MAC but names none beyond WARNINGs (NOT STATED). Reading: we run only CSMA, so we send the WARNINGs required above and report the finding to the operator through management and logging; we never change MAC mode or channel automatically.
notes: Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: Reason value for WTRP D_PDUs: Annex J says an unrecognised D_PDU draws reason 'Unrecognised D_PDU type' (0). WTRP D_PDUs are EXTENSION (type 13) D_PDUs, a type every Ed4 node recognises; Ed4 Annex C gives reason 4 'Unrecognized D_PDU Extension Type' for an unknown extended type and says reason 0 is expected only from Ed3 peers, since all 16 types are now used. Reading: a WTRP or other unknown extended type draws a WARNING with RECEIVED FRAME TYPE 13 and reason 4; reason 0 is used only for the unknown type 6 subtype case of J.4.1.1.
notes: Ed4 C Table C-3, pp.C-55 to C-56; C.7.5.1, p.C-110; plan 4.4 extended-types row, which already chooses reason 4.

requirement: Addressing scope: J.4.1.1 asks for a WARNING for any WTRP D_PDU received, while the Annex C conditions for unrecognised types and extended types cover D_PDUs addressed to the receiving node. WTRP token traffic on a shared channel is often addressed to other nodes. Reading: send the WARNING when the WTRP D_PDU is addressed to this node, to a group address this node belongs to, or to broadcast; do not answer WTRP D_PDUs addressed to other individual nodes. Never answer a WARNING with a WARNING.
notes: Ed4 C.4.15, p.C-56 conditions 1 and 5 (addressed to the receiving node), condition 4 (no addressing qualifier) and shall (10). Accepted by the coordinator as proposed (2026-11-07): avoids warning storms on a shared channel. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: Unknown type 6 subtype: Annex J asks for a WARNING (reason 0), while Annex C says a node should answer an unknown EOW with an UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR EOW (type 3). Reading: do both. The WARNING meets the Annex J shall and the type 3 EOW follows the Annex C should (plan 4.3 EOW row). Acknowledgement of the MANAGEMENT D_PDU itself follows the Annex C rows.
notes: Ed4 C.6.3, p.C-70. Not listed in plan 4.4.

requirement: Receive-only nodes (for example under emission control) never transmit, so they cannot disturb a multi-node network whatever its MAC mode.
Transmitting nodes may use this to embed broadcast or multicast traffic for receive-only nodes, as Annex A A.1.1 intends.
notes: Our non-ARQ broadcast and multicast service.

requirement: The MAC layer may be mapped onto the HF channel in one of three ways: fixed frequency, scheduled frequency, or ALE for all nodes.
notes: Text before J.5.1; the J.5 heading is missing. We use fixed frequency (profile CSMA Fixed Frequency, plan 4.1).

requirement: Fixed frequency: every node uses one agreed frequency; simple and robust, for example for surface-wave networks.
notes: Our profile.

requirement: All nodes on the network must use the same agreed frequency and, where STANAG 5069 wideband HF is in use, the same chosen bandwidth.
notes: The text leaves open whether its shall covers the frequency, the bandwidth or both; we apply it to both. We treat our 110D Appendix D waveform as the 5069 case (assumption A1, plan D1); frequency and bandwidth are network-wide configuration.

requirement: Scheduled frequency: all nodes follow an agreed schedule of frequencies, for example separate day and night frequencies.
reason: not part of our profile CSMA Fixed Frequency (plan 4.1)

requirement: Annex B already provides on-demand ALE linking for point-to-point and multicast traffic.
reason: ALE is not in our profile CSMA Fixed Frequency (plan 4.3)

requirement: Alternatively ALE can be run for all nodes and managed at the MAC layer, holding one channel open for CSMA or WTRP so a linked pair does not block other nodes.
reason: ALE is not in our profile CSMA Fixed Frequency (plan 4.3)

requirement: With ALE at MAC level the channel should be closed and reopened from time to time, to choose the best channel and bring in nodes missed before.
reason: ALE is not in our profile CSMA Fixed Frequency (plan 4.3)
notes: Text says it 'is important'; no shall.

requirement: Ed4 change: Annex J now covers networks of any number of nodes, not only two.
notes: Change list at the end of the annex; the heading is missing. Ed4 main Table 3, p.16 nevertheless says no significant change for Annex J.

requirement: Ed4 change: normative references to Annex M (a placeholder) were removed.
Ed4 change: CSMA is now required for point-to-point operation, settling an Ed3 inconsistency about whether the MACS adds anything.
Ed4 change: a section on mapping to the channel and on ALE use was added.

Annex J versus Annex R: Annex J requires P2P to use CSMA per Annex K and lists that as an Ed4 change, while Annex R says the MAC layer is optional and not needed on a channel with only two nodes. Reading: follow Annex J; CSMA per Annex K runs whatever the number of nodes, including two.
notes: Ed4 J.3.1, p.J-3; J change item 3, p.J-9; Ed4 R, p.R-4. Annex R is not implemented (plan 4.3). Plan 4.1.

requirement: J.3.1 allows 'some simplification' of Annex K for two nodes without saying what. Reading: the only two-node simplifications are those Annex K itself defines (zero LBT wait, K.3.2.2 rule 1); whether a contention wait still follows is settled by K-0109 (decision D7).
notes: Plan 4.4 CSMA two-node row; D7.

requirement: WTRP token EOW: Annex J asks for WARNINGs only for WTRP D_PDU types and for type 6 subtypes, but the WTRP token is an EOW of type 13 that can ride in the header of any D_PDU, and Annex C drops EOW 13 and 14 when WTRP is not in use. Reading: an EOW 13 in a type 6 MANAGEMENT D_PDU addressed to us draws a WARNING with reason 3, as J-0038 requires (EOW 13 is a known type, so no UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR EOW); in any other D_PDU it is ignored, and the D_PDU is processed normally. Either way the channel analysis takes it as evidence of WTRP in use and reports it as J-0051 says.
notes: Ed4 L Token Protocol, p.L-17; Ed4 C Table C-4, p.C-66; Ed4 C.7.5.1, p.C-110; Ed4 C.6.3, p.C-70. Addressing scope as J-0053. Not listed in plan 4.4.
